rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran; three decision_needed items remain (the attempt cap against EPMCDME-16545's retry criterion, the end metric's duplicate window against exactly-once, and the missing security sign-off), and reachability of CR-006, CR-008 and CR-009 is unconfirmed. Five items were deferred to code-review-deferred.local.md (state-file mode, record path validation, poll-time sends under the invalid-auth mark, the failed poll window, the unchanged agent session id). 31 candidates were dismissed as noise, including the code-quality file-size and JSDoc rows, which the guide does not make blocking.

findings.title: Attribution change lacks security sign-off evidence
findings.problem: The PR's Impact section states that the folder-switch attribution change needs security-review sign-off before merge, and neither the diff nor the spec artifact evidences it.
findings.impact: Attribution data could change without the review the PR itself requires. Reachability unconfirmed: this cannot be judged from code, so the sign-off may exist elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Obtain and record the security-review sign-off for the attribution change in the PR before merge, or have the PR owner state that it is not required.

findings.title: Attempt cap drops unsent end metric untried
findings.problem: deliverLocked renames a record unsent once deliveryAttempts reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS, without trying a send. Finalization counts as attempt 1 and a network failure keeps its attempt, so a failed finalize plus two failed daemon starts means the next start drops the record even with connectivity back. An attempt is also spent when the daemon is killed after the counter save and before any send. The cap is in the PR and pinned by a test, while EPMCDME-16545 asks for a retry after connectivity returns, including after a restart.
findings.impact: The session-end metric is permanently lost across an outage that spans restarts, which is the defect the ticket describes; required criterion is only partially met.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the ticket's retry after restored connectivity overrides the 3-attempt cap. If it does, make one real send before dropping and do not spend an attempt on a start that made no request or on a network failure; if the cap stands, amend the ticket's acceptance criterion.

findings.title: New runtime modules break kebab-case naming
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires kebab-case.ts file names and its Pre-Commit Checklist requires naming conventions followed. DesktopSessionDelivery.ts and DesktopSessionMetrics.ts are new in this change and PascalCase, while the two other modules split out alongside them conform. PascalCase siblings already exist in the directory, with no documented exception.
findings.impact: A documented checklist rule no automated gate enforces is broken on new files, the cheapest point to conform.
findings.recommendation: Rename to desktop-session-delivery.ts and desktop-session-metrics.ts and update their imports in DesktopTelemetryRuntime.ts, DesktopSessionDelivery.ts and any test that references them.

findings.title: End metric can be sent twice after crash
findings.problem: endMetricSentAt is saved after sendSessionEnd returns, so a process cut between the server's 200 and the save re-sends the metric on the next pass. The code's own comment admits it, and stopDaemon's SIGKILL 5 s after SIGTERM is one live way to hit the window. EPMCDME-16545 asks for delivery exactly once.
findings.impact: A duplicate session-end metric reaches analytics in that window; the required criterion is only partially met, and the PR does not disclose the duplicate case.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether at-least-once in this crash window satisfies the criterion. If not, add a server-side idempotency key for the end metric; if so, amend the criterion and name the duplicate case in the PR.

findings.title: Stop path's in-memory activity is untested
findings.problem: regression-gap: stop() passes tracked.lastSeenActivityAt to finalizeSession, but no stop test has in-memory activity newer than the saved checkpoint; the touch-without-write case exists only on the inactivity path.
findings.impact: DesktopTelemetryRuntime.stop(), reached from the daemon's SIGTERM cleanup: dropping the argument would report a short end_time and duration, and tests would still pass, contradicting the documented end rule behind EPMCDME-16542.
findings.recommendation: Open a chat, poll, advance the clock, touch the Desktop metadata with no transcript write, poll, then stop; assert reason desktop-daemon-stop, endTime equal to the touched time, and the same end_time on the END metric.

findings.title: Held-back window reopens idle sessions without activity
findings.problem: A reopen lock wait that keeps failing holds lastPollAt back. If that lasts past the inactivity timeout, another session finalized meanwhile is still inside the discovery window, so it is re-tracked from knownSessionIds and retrackSession reopens it with no new activity. finalizeInactive then finalizes it again in the same poll.
findings.impact: Repeated zero-duration end metrics, one per poll, for as long as the lock wait fails. Reachability unconfirmed: it needs one record's lock held for over five minutes, and each request under the lock is bounded.
findings.recommendation: In retrackSession, do not reopen a completed record unless discovered.updatedAt is newer than its saved runtimeCheckpoint.lastSeenActivityAt: return it unchanged and leave it untracked.

findings.title: New record ownership is not tested
findings.problem: regression-gap: buildNewSession spreads daemonOwner(), but every owner assertion in DesktopTelemetryRuntime.test.ts follows a re-track or reads a fixture, and retrackSession assigns the owner on the next transcript change, hiding an omission at creation.
findings.impact: DesktopSessionDelivery.classifyRecord and the CLI start pass: without the owner a single-state session's completed record is never re-delivered and its active record is left for the 72 h legacy close with nothing sent, and tests would still pass.
findings.recommendation: After the first poll of a new chat, with no appended messages, assert the record has ownerPid process.pid and ownerStartedAt processStartedAt(); or test that a never re-tracked record whose END metric failed is re-delivered.

findings.title: Folder switch orphans the old transcript
findings.problem: retrackSession now writes the new path to both correlation.agentSessionFile and runtimeCheckpoint.transcriptPath, so the old folder's transcript is named by neither. readTrackedLogPaths and the ownership index then omit it. The native-loader comment and its tests describe two differing paths, a pair only records saved before this change can hold; every fixture is hand-written and no test drives a real switch.
findings.impact: loadNativeSessions: if the old transcript stays under ~/.claude/projects it is parsed as an untracked claude session tagged native-external, so pre-switch usage can be counted separately or be missing from the CodeMie session's cost. Reachability unconfirmed: whether Desktop leaves the old file in place was not established.
findings.recommendation: Keep the previous transcript paths on the record (for example runtimeCheckpoint.previousTranscriptPaths), read them in recordTranscriptPaths, and add a test driving a real folder switch with the old transcript still on disk, asserting trackedLogPaths and hasOwnershipMarker still include it; or state explicitly that the old transcript is meant to become unowned.

findings.title: Transient companion read fault reads as folder switch
findings.problem: loadCompanionMetadata returns null on any read or parse failure, so discovery falls back to metadata.originCwd, userSelectedFolders, cwd or transcriptDir. retrackSession now treats any differing workingDirectory as a folder switch and overwrites workingDirectory, gitBranch, repository and project, which it stays on until the next transcript change.
findings.impact: A wrong or blank attribution on later deltas and the end metric, if a companion read fails during a re-track, for example while Desktop is writing the file. Reachability unconfirmed: how often Desktop leaves that file unreadable was not established.
findings.recommendation: Do not take over a folder unless the companion metadata was read successfully, and never from the transcriptDir fallback; for example have discovery mark the working directory as a fallback and skip the switch for it.
